verdicts.quote: “For third-party applications that need to access Sentry on behalf of users, Sentry supports OAuth2 with the authorization code grant type.” ([docs.sentry.dev](https://docs.sentry.dev/api/auth/))
verdicts.reason: Sentry documents a public OAuth2 flow suitable for multi-tenant apps; other tokens exist but OAuth2 is the primary method for third‑party apps.

verdicts.quote: “The review process typically takes 4–5 weeks… Only the organization that created the integration can see or install it until it is published.” ([sentry.help](https://www.sentry.help/en/articles/13964035-how-to-submit-a-public-integration-publication-request-in-sentry))
verdicts.reason: While tokens/internal integrations are self‑serve, distributing a public OAuth app to other orgs requires Sentry’s review, so meaningful production use is app‑review gated.

verdicts.quote: “Crons; Dashboards; Discover & Performance; … Events & Issues; … Organizations; … Projects; Releases; Replays; SCIM; … Teams; Users.” ([docs.sentry.io](https://docs.sentry.io/api/))
verdicts.reason: The API covers dozens of resource areas across account, project, and data features, indicating broad surface area.

verdicts.quote: “Sentry MCP Server… Connects AI assistants to Sentry… The base MCP server address is: https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp… All connections use OAuth.” ([mcp.sentry.dev](https://mcp.sentry.dev/))
verdicts.reason: Vendor hosts and documents an official MCP server.
Docs and OAuth exist so it’s buildable, but publishing a multi‑tenant OAuth app requires Sentry’s app review (and API rate limits also apply).
